title: recalledMemories source is built-in Memory Recall, gated by access_vectors — not Long-Term Memory
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:151 'Its output reaches a custom agent only if that agent has the recalledMemories context source enabled'; :206 '`recalledMemories` | Long-Term Memory / vector recall results'; :223 '`recalledMemories` is what connects the Long-Term Memory package to a custom agent'; :364 'a custom agent sees recall output only if its recalledMemories context source is enabled. Long-Term Memory being installed is not sufficient'; assets/custom-agent.template.json:12/:21 (no access_vectors mention)
reality: The only producer of vectorContext.recalledMemories is the built-in Memory Recall (injectMemoryRecallContext -> recallMemories over this chat's past messages) in generate.routes.ts:4835-4905 and retry-agents-route.ts:1214; vectorContext is attached only when some agent has the access_vectors capability (generate.routes.ts:4840, :5198), and agent-executor.ts:2060-2068 builds the <vector_context> block only for agents with access_vectors, filtering recalledMemories by the context source. The editor marks the source requiredCapability 'access_vectors' (AgentEditor.tsx:386-387); en.json ui.agents.agenteditor.contextSource.recalledMemories.description = 'Include memories recalled from earlier in the chat. Needs the Vectors/embeddings ability.' Recall for agents is skipped while Advanced Memory Recall is on (all branches gated !advancedMemoryEnabled). Nothing feeds the Long-Term Memory package vault into this source. Same behavior at v2.4.0.
fix: agents.md: table row -> '`recalledMemories` | Built-in Memory Recall fragments from this chat (embedding retrieval); needs the **Vectors/embeddings** capability (`access_vectors`) and an embedding source; empty while Advanced Memory Recall is on'. Rewrite :151, :223 and the 'wiring that matters' paragraph at :364: the agent needs BOTH `recalledMemories: true` AND `access_vectors` (which also forces its own request); it receives Memory Recall output, not the Long-Term Memory package vault. Drop the claim that recalledMemories connects Long-Term Memory to custom agents. Template _comment_contextSources: add 'recalledMemories also needs the access_vectors capability (settings.customCapabilities.access_vectors = true; UI Vectors/embeddings), which forces its own request; it carries built-in Memory Recall fragments, not the Long-Term Memory vault'.

title: Package install/import/import-policy are privileged — remote devices need ADMIN_SECRET
skill_evidence: absent — references/agents.md:5, :58, :72, :345 describe installing from Download Agents, toggling Allow custom Agent imports and importing agents with no remote-access caveat (the skill gives this caveat for tools in custom-tools.md:257 and extensions.md:66)
reality: capability-packages.routes.ts:205 (update decline), :256 (POST /:id/install), :283 (DELETE /:id); agents.routes.ts:236 (PATCH /import-policy), :242 (POST /import); custom-agent-repositories.routes.ts preview/add/sync/remove all call requirePrivilegedAccess(). privileged-gate.ts: loopback passes; otherwise 403 'ADMIN_SECRET is required for privileged APIs' / 'Invalid or missing X-Admin-Secret header'. title: PUT /toggle/:agentType does not enable or disable anything
reality: agents.routes.ts:561-588: '/** Legacy endpoint retained for compatibility. Agent activation is chat-scoped. */' — for a built-in type it returns the existing config or creates a default one; 404 for unknown types; no enabled flag changes. Per-chat activation lives in chat metadata `enableAgents` + `activeAgentIds` (packages/shared/src/types/chat.ts:332, :340); createAgentConfigSchema marks `enabled` 'Legacy compatibility only'.
fix: agents.md:473 -> '`PUT /toggle/:agentType` — legacy: materializes a built-in's config (returns or creates it); it does not toggle anything. To run an agent in a chat, set that chat's metadata `enableAgents: true` and add the type to `activeAgentIds`.'

title: Agent Budget ranges and clamping misdescribed
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:270-277 'constants in packages/shared/src/types/agent.ts ...'; '`contextSize` | 5 | 1 – `MAX_AGENT_CONTEXT_MESSAGES`'; '`maxTokens` | 4096 | 128 – 32768'; '`normalizeAgentContextSize` clamps out-of-range values back to the default'; template :24 'range 128-32768'
reality: MAX_AGENT_CONTEXT_MESSAGES = 200 is a private const in packages/server/src/services/agents/agent-executor.ts:84 (not shared); normalizeAgentContextSize (:325-330) returns the default 5 only for non-numeric or <1, and clamps >200 down to 200; editor input min 1 max 200 (AgentEditor.tsx ~2862). maxTokens: only the 128 floor is enforced (client clampAgentMaxTokens AgentEditor.tsx:251-253; server normalizeAgentMaxTokens agent-executor.ts:580-585); MAX_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS = 32768 is exported (types/agent.ts:592) but referenced nowhere; the real ceiling is the connection's max-tokens override and the model's max output (applyAgentMaxTokensCaps :732-738).
fix: Table: contextSize range '1–200 (MAX_AGENT_CONTEXT_MESSAGES, server agent-executor.ts)'; maxTokens 'min 128; 32768 is the documented ceiling but not enforced — the connection's max-tokens override and the model's max output cap it'. Replace the clamping sentence: 'values above 200 clamp to 200; blank, non-numeric or <1 fall back to 5'. Mirror in template _comment_budget.

title: Regency example uses a nonexistent {{message}} macro and an unsupported 'wire to rewrite agent' path
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:457 promptTemplate ends 'The passage:\n{{message}}'; :462 '(if wired to a rewrite agent — `continuity` or `prose-guardian`) trigger rewrites on issues'
reality: macro-engine.ts has no `message` macro (catalog :437-531 lists {{input}} for the latest user message; unknown tokens are left as-is, :3104); post-processing agents receive the reply automatically as <assistant_response> (agent-executor.ts:2864-2867). Built-in rewrite agents only merge with each other (prose-guardian-settings.ts:9 REWRITE_AGENT_TYPES = prose-guardian/continuity/html, mergePairedBuiltInRewriteAgents); Turn Data Access exposes only pre-gen injections and parallel results to post-processing agents — no mechanism feeds a custom agent's post-processing output into Prose Guardian/Continuity.
fix: Drop '{{message}}' (end with 'Check the assistant response you were given.'), and replace :462 with: 'It runs after each reply; its output is cached and injected into the next turn's prompt (or exposed via Add as Prompt Section / {{agent::historical_accuracy_regency}}). To have it fix text itself, make it a `text_rewrite` agent instead.'
